presentation.label: Cleaner recorder loops
presentation.summary: Fix recorder-buffer voice reprime, counter resets, alternating recording lengths and sound-on-sound zero samples at the loop boundary.
presentation.overview: Fix recorder-buffer voice reprime, counter resets, alternating recording lengths and sound-on-sound zero samples at the loop boundary. This source import remains a draft until composition and release qualification are complete.
highlights: Automatic when included in a qualified image; there is no menu, knob or effect slot. Remove the module when building to restore stock behavior.
Applies to Flex playback of recorder buffers, including sound-on-sound. Ordinary sample playback fallback paths are retained.
Uses the stock tempo, arm sample and recorder length. It does not run a separate clock.
usage: Use a disposable project and assign a Flex track to its own recorder buffer.
Set RLEN to 16 at 128 BPM and place recording and playback trigs at the start of the bar; for sound-on-sound set SRC3 to that track.
Record a sustained tone and listen across successive wraps, then repeat after stopping and restarting transport.
Compare with stock using the same project, tempo and sample. A fractional-sample loop can still repeat or skip one sample at a wrap.

limitations: Draft source: not selectable in the configurator until release checks pass.
Automatic when included in a qualified image; there is no menu, knob or effect slot. Remove the module when building to restore stock behavior.
Applies to Flex playback of recorder buffers, including sound-on-sound. Ordinary sample playback fallback paths are retained.
Uses the stock tempo, arm sample and recorder length. It does not run a separate clock.
At fractional bar lengths, a wrap can still repeat or skip one sample; this does not guarantee a perfectly seamless loop at every tempo.
Eight hook sites and eleven pool-base literals must participate in the common builder allocation ledger; catalog publication and native/browser composition remain pending.

The native spacing algorithm can choose a loop length one sample off after several minutes at short RLEN values: 953/13,279 ideal consecutive-arm cases failed. At 197 BPM and RLEN 1, the first tested failure was five minutes. RLEN 16 had no failures in the tested integer-BPM sweep through four hours; arbitrary fractional tempo or arm histories are not qualified.

processing.label: ColdFire native paths
processing.display: Measured model cycles; chip wall-clock pending
processing.conditions: MCF5206E core-cycle model, cache-hit zero-wait; not MCF54455 chip timing. Synthetic stock callbacks exclude their actual work. Conservative V4 code-cycle path bounds exclude cache, bus and interrupt contention; see TESTING.md.

impact.conditions: Source estimate for eight audio tracks; no added DSP program. Complete timing and placement remain pending.

cpu.rationale: Finite ColdFire hook paths with bounded eight-track loops; native paths and stack peaks were measured. The independent long-run spacing oracle has a measured failure, so low cost does not imply correct loop spacing.

dsp.rationale: No new DSP program; existing voice and FX dispatch is retained.

memory.rationale: Small authored ROM patches and reused stock state; no new audio buffer allocation.

tests.summary: All 24 assembly-oracle checks passed. Short-arm and hold/seek native probes passed; the independent long-run spacing sweep FAILED in 953 of 13,279 cases. RLEN 16 passed 1,897 tested long-run cases. Publication remains blocked; see TESTING.md.
